reviews.comment: Hossain is an amazing professor.
His teaching is heavily focused on student learning.

The course allows for retakes, but without many practice problems, it's hard to improve. Homework tends to be more difficult than exams, so it's not great study material. Lectures are mostly conceptual, while exams are worked-out problems, so there's a mismatch b/w what's taught and what's tested.

I really appreciated Zubaer. Cares deeply, wants us to learn, and remembers what it is like to be a busy student. He allowed exam/quiz retakes (even though they were still hard). Lectures are entertaining and beneficial. Final project is insane start early on that.

I don't think there is a negative thing about him. He's beyond generous with credit, he doesn't assign a lot of busy work, very accessible and it's obvious he cares, and I wouldn't say his exams are that hard.

This is the best 305 professor at A&M. He gives so many resources for you to be successful. His lectures are in depth and there are plenty of examples. He has a clear method of teaching. The exams were open note. The end-of-semester project was not that hard. There is no reason to choose any other professor.

He is very clearly passionate about the material and does his best to ensure everyone understands him. I genuinely enjoyed his class.

Tough (and few) HW, easy quizzes, and 2% attendance bonus.
First midterm isn't bad, final is ok but super long, project is time consuming.
The A is super achievable as long as you don't skip the homeworks (oops)
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good, caring prof who really wants to teach. HWs were long and tough, quizzes doable, exams challenging. Gives 4% bonus, drops worst HW/quiz, and offers a remake midterm. Open book exams (except GBT). Uses OneNote—no slides, and notes can be hard to follow if you miss class. Overall good prof, but tough exams. I lost the A mostly due to myself.

This is a great class and he is a great professor. The homeworks are long and pretty difficult, but there were only four of them for our class. There were only two mandatory exams, which weren't bad. He explained all the concepts pretty well and took time to answer questions and assist students.

One of the best professors I've had at TAMU. He actively will take feedback from the students and immediately implement adjustments to the course to ensure each student is learning optimally. He is able to teach to material effectively without having to rely on an exam-heavy grading criteria. Would definitely take this professor again.

Took Zubaer intentionally since I had him for 305 as well. He's one of A&M's absolute gifts. Willing to go above and beyond for students. Always asks students for their input and opinion, tailors his class notes to our needs. All of the projects/papers were practical with real world applications. If he's available, he's a must take professor.

This FEM course had solid math for grad-level students, but true learning came from assignments and projects. The instructor, teaching it for the first time, moved slowly but made genuine efforts. Scripting is essential, and while not explicitly covered in lectures, much of the logic must be figured out independently.

Great Professor. He really knows his stuff, and if you put in the work, then you will too. Get ready to code in either Python or MATLAB. Learning LaTeX will be of incredible use to you. This course is no joke, but you will definitely understand, and be able to use and modify FEM code at the end. You do things by hand, then by coding it.

Fall 2024 Review: Dr. Hossain is an excellent professor! He truly cares about his students, has good knowledge he wants to share, and is always open to questions. His class is very well structured and he tries to help students understand the concepts by using simulations and real world examples to put things into perspective. Take him!

Zubaer is a great professor that really cares about his students understanding the material. He is a lenient grader and will help you with homework and projects if you reach out to him. He makes all his lecture notes, codes, and equation sheets available. Make sure you attend lecture because the class will be very hard to follow if you don't.

Professor Hossain was an amazing professor for MEEN 368.  He is one of the most caring professors I have had at Texas A&M.  He really cares about his students and wants his students to succeed.  He does a great job integrating real world applications into his lectures/projects.  I would absolutely recommend taking Professor Hossain for MEEN 368!

Hossain really values people's understanding of the material over the grade they receive and it shows. Some of the quizzes he gave were kind of difficult, but there's always ways to get your grade up if need be. Quizzes and Finals were all online and he lets people use any notes they want on them. Easy A, understanding is on you though.

his accent is a little thicker than most but not hard to understand if you pay attention. he is a very very very kind professor please protect this man. he cares alot about making sure you understand the material rather than the grade. grading is very very generous and though the class can be tough he tries his hardest to make it easy for you.

Hossain really does care about if you learn the material and not so much about grades (in a good way). If you have a tangible grasp on the subject, he will help you grow and grades leniently. He explains clearly and answers questions well. He also makes himself available outside of class for those who needs help. Truly a prof that cares.

One in a million kind of professor. Passionate, kind, and willingly to go above and beyond to help others. Clearly goes through material, ensuring students know what is going on. Always willing to take questions and feedback. Exams, quizzes,(both open note), and homework go through material that is taught so if you prepare you do well. Awesome guy
